ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

A plasma-cell inclusion

A biopsy from a chronically inflamed mucosal site contains numerous plasma cells. Several cells have rounded eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions composed of retained immunoglobulin in distended endoplasmic reticulum. Which name is used for these inclusions?

  1. Hemosiderin granules
  2. Lipofuscin granules
  3. Russell bodies
  4. Heinz bodies
  5. Councilman bodies
Answer and explanation

Russell bodies

Russell bodies represent immunoglobulin accumulation within dilated rough endoplasmic reticulum of plasma cells.

Option explanations

Russell bodies: Russell bodies represent immunoglobulin accumulation within dilated rough endoplasmic reticulum of plasma cells.

Heinz bodies: Heinz bodies are denatured hemoglobin in erythrocytes.

Councilman bodies: Councilman bodies are apoptotic hepatocytes.

Hemosiderin granules: Hemosiderin stores iron.

Lipofuscin granules: Lipofuscin is residual pigment associated with cellular aging and oxidative injury.
